basics.name: Anton Dziatkovskii
basics.label: Developer activation for frontier platforms · operating lead, Palo Alto AI Research Lab (an independent lab)
basics.summary: I've done developer activation for a frontier platform before — when smart contracts were where LLM agents are now. Classically trained in CS security (MEPhI), programming in Python and C++, eleven years as a hired operating executive (COO/CTO) at a startup incubator and software house (since 2015; in crypto since 2015 — supported early Ethereum and Cardano fundraising efforts in Japan), author of two preprints on multi-agent stability. A superconnector with a builder's toolkit: a decade-deep network of founders, builders, engineers and investors (10,000+ founder calls, 2,000+ institutional-investor calls) — and I automate my own connector work end-to-end, from a self-built CRM to today's AI-agent fleet. Today I run a production multi-machine Claude fleet in public — and write the operating manual as I go. Built with Claude as implementation collaborator; I own problem framing, architecture, evaluation, product decisions and final QA. Based between Palo Alto, CA — the heart of Silicon Valley — and Sintra, PT. US O-1 visa active and EU citizen (Polish passport): authorized to work in the US and anywhere in the EU immediately, no visa sponsorship required.

Operate a six-machine production fleet at an independent lab, with public failure reports and reproducible tests. Programming: Python and C++. US O-1 active; Polish citizen; no US/EU sponsorship required.
x_role_summaries.coo: Operating executive with 11 years at an APAC incubator and software house. Managed 40+ developers as product owner; built an in-house CRM used daily by up to 30 operators. Ran startup cohorts, advisor matching and enterprise advisory, drawing on five years building Salesforce and Microsoft Navision systems. Combine operations leadership with hands-on programming in Python and C++. US O-1 active; Polish citizen; no US/EU sponsorship required.

work.name: Palo Alto AI Research Lab
work.summary: Independent lab started in 2023 in Palo Alto, CA; grew a community of 100+ AI practitioners, including Stanford researchers and big-tech engineers. Production multi-machine Claude fleet run in public: claw-consensus (reproducible multi-machine agent consensus, offline demo, published evals, FAILURE-MODES.md), verbatim-citation-gate (zero-token gate + burden-of-proof judge that catches fabricated RAG citations, MIT), agent-control-plane-casebook (reproducible control-plane failures from the production fleet — each case ships a deterministic repro, a runnable red test and an upstream bug report), the operating manual written day by day (相棒 AIBŌ · The Partner).
highlights: Red-team my own production agent fleet and publish the result: a written threat model (8 assets, 6 trust boundaries, 10 untrusted input surfaces, 9 residual risks carrying numbers) mapped onto OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications (2025) and MITRE ATLAS by exact identifier — published together with its holes: 15 ATLAS techniques reproduced on my own stand, 10 more named as applicable and untested, 12 ATLAS mitigations implemented and 8 explicitly not (github.com/tonydzi/agent-fleet-red-team)

Measured the fleet's human-approval gate as two separate numbers rather than one accuracy figure (2026-10-08): 100% refusal across 49 must-ask actions, 50% over-refusal across 42 benign ones, and 71.4% rule coverage — 14 of the 49 reach a human only because the default is fail-closed, each one named in the report. Six-way mutation suite, shown failing on broken code before it was shown passing. The same gate on real traffic: 2,879 high-risk firings in 90 days, 0 asks expired unanswered

Reproduced an indirect prompt-injection chain end to end on my own stand (github.com/tonydzi/leash-poc): one poisoned string, four input surfaces, four agents, 24 requests. Naive fleet exfiltrated 168 bytes, deleted 5 files, rotated 4 production keys and spawned 4 admin sub-agents; behind a single independent authorization boundary, zero on all five — with the user's work still completed. 27 hash-chained decisions, chain verified after SIGKILL mid-run

Merged into microsoft/semantic-kernel (#14371, Oct 2026): closed the check-time/use-time gap in the OpenAPI plugin's anti-SSRF validator. The request now goes to the exact address the validator vetted, so on the plugin's built-in HTTP client a DNS-rebinding hostname can no longer pass the check and then reach an internal address (scoped as hardening; caller-supplied clients and proxies stay out of scope); TLS is still verified against the hostname, no new dependency, 12 tests including one that drives real httpx + httpcore through a simulated rebind

Run an evidence-first reliability program across the AI-agent open-source ecosystem: reproducible cross-project probes, mutation-tested reviews of other people's pull requests, and bug reports that arrive with a deterministic reproduction and a regression test demonstrated failing on the unfixed code

Review accepted by the author, not merely posted — google/adk-python#6957, an OAuth2 client secret leaking over three endpoints: the mutation matrix showed which of the project's own tests stayed green, and the author adopted all three findings within six hours (“genuinely one of the most useful reviews I've gotten on this PR”)

Failure classes driven to an upstream fix: google/adk-python#6887 (session ids normalised on write but not on read) fixed from the report; #6941, filed with a measured root cause, was labelled core, assigned to a maintainer and answered by two third-party pull requests
Credited in a third-party release 40 hours after the report — headroom v2.0.8: “reported by @tonydzi”

Scope of the program since Jul 2026 (verified 2026-10-08): 40 pull requests merged into 25 third-party engineering projects — Microsoft Semantic Kernel, Model Context Protocol Go SDK, UK AISI inspect_ai, QwenLM/qwen-code, google-gemini/cookbook, bytedance/deer-flow, fastmcp, agno, pydantic/logfire, deepset-ai/haystack-integrations — plus 65 issues filed upstream

The program runs unattended: 13 daily autonomous lanes on the fleet (code review, live-install documentation QA, issue-first bug reports, thread watch), with human approval gates on anything irreversible
